title: Isaiah 40 — Comfort my people: the voice in the wilderness and the one who measured the skies

verdicts.reasoning: naḥămû naḥămû ʿammî yōʾmar ʾĕlōhêḵem: plural imperatives, 'your God'. Exact.

dabbᵉrû ʿal-lēḇ yᵉrûšālaim ... kî mālᵉʾāh ṣᵉḇāʾāh kî nirṣāh ʿăwōnāh ... kip̄layim: 'her warfare is ended', 'her iniquity is pardoned', 'double' exact. Non-blocking: the note states as fact that kip̄layim means 'full equivalent, not twice'; present this as one interpretation, since many take 'double' literally.
qôl qôrēʾ bammiḏbār pannû dereḵ YHWH: the accents (zaqef on qôrēʾ) join 'in the wilderness' to 'prepare', and the line follows MT against the LXX/Gospel phrasing. Exact.
kol-geyʾ yinnāśēʾ ... wᵉhāyāh heʿāqōḇ lᵉmîšôr wᵉhārᵉḵāsîm lᵉḇiqʿāh: exact.
wᵉniḡlāh kᵉḇôḏ YHWH ...: 'the glory of YHWH' under central kavod-yhwh; exact.

citations: Ulrich & Flint, Qumran Cave 1.II: The Isaiah Scrolls (DJD 32, 2010), ad loc. (1QIsaᵃ ואומרה)
verdicts.reasoning: Disputed vs ASV 'goodliness'. qôl ʾōmēr qᵉrāʾ wᵉʾāmar ... wᵉḵol-ḥasdô kᵉṣîṣ haśśāḏeh: MT 'and he said' kept, 1QIsaᵃ/LXX 'and I said' reported. Human ḥeseḏ 'constancy' (NRSV) is lexically right; ASV 'goodliness' follows LXX doxa. Defensible.
kî rûaḥ YHWH nāšᵉḇāh bô: the wind that withers grass, 'the breath of YHWH' (ASV/NRSV); 'the people is grass' exact.
ûḏᵉḇar-ʾĕlōhênû yāqûm lᵉʿôlām: exact.
mᵉḇaśśereṯ ṣiyyôn: ASV's objective reading kept, and the appositional NRSV/NJPS 'O Zion, herald of good tidings' honestly recorded; both standard.
hinnēh ʾăḏōnāy YHWH bᵉḥāzāq yāḇôʾ: 'the Lord YHWH' (Tetragrammaton pointed as ʾĕlōhîm); exact.
kᵉrōʿeh ʿeḏrô yirʿeh ... ʿālôṯ yᵉnahēl: exact.
mî-māḏaḏ bᵉšoʿŏlô mayim wᵉšāmayim bazzereṯ tikkēn: 'marked off the skies with a span' applies the creation-register rule; exact otherwise.
mî-ṯikkēn ʾeṯ-rûaḥ YHWH: 'directed' (ASV/NRSV), lower-case 'the spirit of YHWH' (NRSV). Defensible.
ʾeṯ-mî nôʿāṣ wayᵉḇînēhû ...: exact.
hēn gôyim kᵉmar middᵉlî ... ʾiyyîm kaddaq yiṭṭôl: exact.
ûlᵉḇānôn ʾên dê bāʿēr wᵉḥayyāṯô ʾên dê ʿôlāh: exact.
mēʾep̄es wāṯōhû neḥšᵉḇû-lô: 'less than nothing and emptiness'; exact.
wᵉʾel-mî tᵉḏammᵉyûn ʾēl: standalone ʾēl 'God' (ASV/NRSV); exact.
happesel nāsaḵ ḥārāš ... ûrᵉṯuqôṯ kesep̄ ṣôrēp̄: 'The carved image!' as exclamation; exact.

Disputed vs ASV 'impoverished'. hamsukkān tᵉrûmāh ʿēṣ lōʾ-yirqaḇ yiḇḥār: mᵉsukkān is the Akkadian tree-name musukkannu (HALOT 'Dalbergia sissoo'), with no consonantal change; the skn 'poor' derivation is obsolete. 'sissoo wood' is the precise identification; 'mulberry' (NRSV/NJPS) is recorded. Defensible. Non-blocking: the CAD page range could not be verified by the Reviewer; cite CAD by lemma if unsure.

Canon-cited. hălôʾ hăḇînōṯem môsᵉḏôṯ hāʾāreṣ: ASV's ellipsis reading ('from the foundations') kept, and the object reading the canon quotes is set out as an equally standard construal. Lens check passed: the line takes the reading that does not favour the canon.

hayyōšēḇ ʿal-ḥûḡ hāʾāreṣ ... hannôṭeh kaddōq šāmayim: 'circle of the earth', 'like a curtain … like a tent' exact; 'skies' in the creation register. Lens check: the note correctly declines any claim about the earth's shape.
hannôṯēn rôzᵉnîm lᵉʾāyin šōp̄ᵉṭê ʾereṣ kattōhû ʿāśāh: exact.
ʾap̄ bal-niṭṭāʿû ... ûsᵉʿārāh kaqqaš tiśśāʾēm: 'Scarcely … when' exact.
wᵉʾel-mî ṯᵉḏammᵉyûnî wᵉʾešweh yōʾmar qāḏôš: exact.

Disputed (draft 'shaped'). mî-ḇārāʾ ʾēlleh hammôṣîʾ ḇᵉmispār ṣᵉḇāʾām: 'who created these?' is the lexical and versional consensus and correct; the escalated cross-corpus question is F1. Non-blocking: the note says bārāʾ takes 'never a material'; say 'never an accusative of material', since the heavens and earth are objects at 42:5; 45:12, 18.
nistᵉrāh ḏarkî mēYHWH ûmēʾĕlōhay mišpāṭî yaʿăḇôr: exact.

Disputed (draft 'who shapes'). ʾĕlōhê ʿôlām YHWH bôrēʾ qᵉṣôṯ hāʾāreṣ: participle in apposition rendered as the title 'the Creator' (ASV); 'the everlasting God' as construct epithet. Correct; F1 governs the cross-corpus question.
nōṯēn layyāʿēp̄ kōaḥ ...: exact.
wᵉyiʿăp̄û nᵉʿārîm wᵉyiḡāʿû ...: exact.
wᵉqôwê YHWH yaḥălîp̄û ḵōaḥ yaʿălû ʾēḇer kannᵉšārîm: exact.

reviewerReport.lensLeakageCheck: Checked all 31 lines. The canon-cited 40:21 keeps the ellipsis reading that does not favour the canon's quotation. 40:22 renders ḥûḡ as 'circle' with no claim about shape. 40:26 'who created these?' replaces the draft's craft verb 'shaped', removing a workshop overtone. reviewerReport.escalationReportAdjustments: Initial verdicts were formed before opening wave-i2-editor-report.md. The report's F1 adds that HALOT assigns the Piel to a separate homonym, which agrees with the Reviewer's view. No verdict changed.

founderDecisionRecommendations.F1-bara: Ratify 'create' / 'Creator' for all 14 Isaiah sites (overlay bara-create-isaiah). Yes, the Genesis 'shape' should be reviewed at the next Genesis pass. Reasons: (1) the Qal/Niphal never takes an accusative of material and the lexica gloss it 'create' (BDB; HALOT brʾ I; Bernhardt TDOT 2; Schmidt THAT 1). (2) The central bara rationale's 'Piel "cut out, fashion"' is the separate homonym 'cut down, clear (forest)' (Josh 17:15, 18; Ezek 23:47; HALOT). Its '(Gesenius §17)' locator is wrong as a GKC reference, since GKC §17 treats Qere/Ketiv. (3) The central yatsar entry glosses yāṣar 'form, shape, fashion (as a potter)', so 'shape' for bārāʾ already collides with the potter's verb even in Genesis. (4) The canon itself uses 'créés, formés et faits' (Isa 43:7). Corpus finding: AMO-WOH-4:13 already renders bôrēʾ rûaḥ 'shapes the wind', an extension of the Genesis 'shape' outside the central appliesTo that is now inconsistent with Isaiah. Review it together with the Genesis decision. Options for the Genesis review: re-render 'create' and keep the bārāʾ/ʿāśāh/yāṣar distinction as create/make/form (the Isaiah model), or keep 'shape' but downgrade the central entry to speculative with a corrected rationale.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F4-divine-ruach: Accept the genre-based split: lower-case 'spirit' in Isaiah's endowment/outpouring poetry and 'ruach' in Kings/Ezekiel agent narratives. The weak point is Ezekiel's own endowment/outpouring verses: 37:14 'I will put my ruach in you' is published, and 36:27 and 39:29 are not yet translated in this data. These share Isaiah's sense rather than the 'agent that lifts' sense that justifies transliteration. At the next Ezekiel pass, decide whether those few sites should move to 'my spirit' or stay 'ruach' for in-book consistency. Either way, add reciprocal cross-references 44:3 ↔ Ezek 37:14 now, and to 39:29 once it is translated. Do not transliterate in Isaiah.

paragraphs.text: נַחֲמ֥וּ נַחֲמ֖וּ עַמִּ֑י יֹאמַ֖ר אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם׃

i18n.en: Comfort, comfort my people, says your God.
i18n.he: נַחֲמ֥וּ נַחֲמ֖וּ עַמִּ֑י יֹאמַ֖ר אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם׃

notes.official: *naḥămû naḥămû ʿammî* “Comfort, comfort my people” opens the second part of the book (chs. 40–55, “Second Isaiah”), set among the exiles in Babylon in the sixth century (Westermann, *Isaiah 40–66*, OTL 1969; Blenkinsopp, *Isaiah 40–55*, AB 19A, 2002). The imperatives are plural, addressed to an unnamed group of heralds, often taken to be the divine council (compare the plural address of 6:8). *ʾĕlōhêḵem* is “your God,” the overlay’s rendering for suffixed *ʾĕlōhîm*, now applied to Second Isaiah.

paragraphs.text: דַּבְּר֞וּ עַל־לֵ֤ב יְרֽוּשָׁלִַ֙ם֙ וְקִרְא֣וּ אֵלֶ֔יהָ כִּ֤י מָֽלְאָה֙ צְבָאָ֔הּ כִּ֥י נִרְצָ֖ה עֲוֺנָ֑הּ כִּ֤י לָקְחָה֙ מִיַּ֣ד יְהוָ֔ה כִּפְלַ֖יִם בְּכָל־חַטֹּאתֶֽיהָ׃ (ס)

i18n.en: Speak to the heart of Jerusalem, and call out to her that her warfare is ended, that her iniquity is pardoned, that she has received from the hand of YHWH double for all her sins.
i18n.he: דַּבְּר֞וּ עַל־לֵ֤ב יְרֽוּשָׁלִַ֙ם֙ וְקִרְא֣וּ אֵלֶ֔יהָ כִּ֤י מָֽלְאָה֙ צְבָאָ֔הּ כִּ֥י נִרְצָ֖ה עֲוֺנָ֑הּ כִּ֤י לָקְחָה֙ מִיַּ֣ד יְהוָ֔ה כִּפְלַ֖יִם בְּכָל־חַטֹּאתֶֽיהָ׃ (ס)

notes.official: *kî mālʾāh ṣᵉḇāʾāh* “that her warfare is ended”: *ṣāḇāʾ* is military service or forced labour, the hard term of exile. *kip̄layim* “double” is the full equivalent, the punishment matching the guilt, not twice what was due (Westermann). *ʿăwōnāh* “her iniquity” is cited to the central `avon-iniquity-cross-corpus-keyword` entry.

paragraphs.text: ק֣וֹל קוֹרֵ֔א בַּמִּדְבָּ֕ר פַּנּ֖וּ דֶּ֣רֶךְ יְהוָ֑ה יַשְּׁרוּ֙ בָּעֲרָבָ֔ה מְסִלָּ֖ה לֵאלֹהֵֽינוּ׃

i18n.en: A voice cries: “In the wilderness prepare the way of YHWH; make straight in the desert a highway for our God.
i18n.he: ק֣וֹל קוֹרֵ֔א בַּמִּדְבָּ֕ר פַּנּ֖וּ דֶּ֣רֶךְ יְהוָ֑ה יַשְּׁרוּ֙ בָּעֲרָבָ֔ה מְסִלָּ֖ה לֵאלֹהֵֽינוּ׃

notes.official: *qôl qôrēʾ* is “A voice cries,” and the voice cries “In the wilderness prepare the way of YHWH.” The Masoretic accents join “in the wilderness” to “prepare,” matching “in the desert” in the parallel line. The LXX, quoted in the Gospels (Mark 1:3), reads “a voice of one crying in the wilderness.” The line follows MT.

paragraphs.text: כָּל־גֶּיא֙ יִנָּשֵׂ֔א וְכָל־הַ֥ר וְגִבְעָ֖ה יִשְׁפָּ֑לוּ וְהָיָ֤ה הֶֽעָקֹב֙ לְמִישׁ֔וֹר וְהָרְכָסִ֖ים לְבִקְעָֽה׃

i18n.en: Every valley shall be lifted up, and every mountain and hill shall be made low; the uneven ground shall become level, and the rough places a plain.
i18n.he: כָּל־גֶּיא֙ יִנָּשֵׂ֔א וְכָל־הַ֥ר וְגִבְעָ֖ה יִשְׁפָּ֑לוּ וְהָיָ֤ה הֶֽעָקֹב֙ לְמִישׁ֔וֹר וְהָרְכָסִ֖ים לְבִקְעָֽה׃

paragraphs.text: וְנִגְלָ֖ה כְּב֣וֹד יְהוָ֑ה וְרָא֤וּ כָל־בָּשָׂר֙ יַחְדָּ֔ו כִּ֛י פִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבֵּֽר׃ (ס)

i18n.en: And the glory of YHWH shall be revealed, and all flesh shall see it together, for the mouth of YHWH has spoken.”
i18n.he: וְנִגְלָ֖ה כְּב֣וֹד יְהוָ֑ה וְרָא֤וּ כָל־בָּשָׂר֙ יַחְדָּ֔ו כִּ֛י פִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבֵּֽר׃ (ס)

notes.official: *kᵉḇôḏ YHWH* “the glory of YHWH” is rendered under the central `kavod-yhwh` entry. In Second Isaiah the glory is revealed on the way back from exile, before “all flesh.”

paragraphs.text: ק֚וֹל אֹמֵ֣ר קְרָ֔א וְאָמַ֖ר מָ֣ה אֶקְרָ֑א כָּל־הַבָּשָׂ֣ר חָצִ֔יר וְכָל־חַסְדּ֖וֹ כְּצִ֥יץ הַשָּׂדֶֽה׃

i18n.en: A voice says: “Cry!” And he said: “What shall I cry?” “All flesh is grass, and all its constancy is like the flower of the field.
i18n.he: ק֚וֹל אֹמֵ֣ר קְרָ֔א וְאָמַ֖ר מָ֣ה אֶקְרָ֑א כָּל־הַבָּשָׂ֣ר חָצִ֔יר וְכָל־חַסְדּ֖וֹ כְּצִ֥יץ הַשָּׂדֶֽה׃

notes.official: Two textual and lexical points. (1) MT *wᵉʾāmar* is “and he said.” The Great Isaiah Scroll (1QIsaᵃ, ואומרה) and the LXX (*kai eipa*) read “and I said,” which makes the passage a first-person call of the prophet, like 6:8, 11, and NRSV adopts it. The line keeps MT (overlay `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`). (2) *wᵉḵol-ḥasdô kᵉṣîṣ haś-śāḏeh* “all its constancy is like the flower of the field.” *ḥeseḏ* attributed to “all flesh” is human loyalty or constancy, as brief as a flower. NRSV has “constancy”; Westermann and Blenkinsopp read “loyalty”; NJPS has “goodness.” ASV’s “goodliness” (beauty) follows the LXX *doxa* (whence 1 Pet 1:24, “all its glory”), not the Hebrew. The covenant-kindness entry (central `chesed-solitary-covenant-kindness`) is not applied to this human use (overlay `lexical-cruxes-wave-i2-isaiah`).

paragraphs.text: יָבֵ֤שׁ חָצִיר֙ נָ֣בֵֽל צִ֔יץ כִּ֛י ר֥וּחַ יְהוָ֖ה נָ֣שְׁבָה בּ֑וֹ אָכֵ֥ן חָצִ֖יר הָעָֽם׃

i18n.en: The grass withers, the flower fades, when the breath of YHWH blows upon it; surely the people is grass.
i18n.he: יָבֵ֤שׁ חָצִיר֙ נָ֣בֵֽל צִ֔יץ כִּ֛י ר֥וּחַ יְהוָ֖ה נָ֣שְׁבָה בּ֑וֹ אָכֵ֥ן חָצִ֖יר הָעָֽם׃

notes.official: *kî rûaḥ YHWH nāšᵉḇāh bô* “when the breath of YHWH blows upon it”: the construct *rûaḥ YHWH* is here the hot desert wind that withers the grass, and the line has “breath” (ASV, NRSV). Six verses later the same construct is “the spirit of YHWH” (v. 13), where it is the divine mind no one can measure. The two renderings mark two senses of one Hebrew phrase (overlay `ruach-divine-spirit-lower-case-isaiah`).

paragraphs.text: יָבֵ֥שׁ חָצִ֖יר נָ֣בֵֽל צִ֑יץ וּדְבַר־אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ יָק֥וּם לְעוֹלָֽם׃ (ס)

i18n.en: The grass withers, the flower fades, but the word of our God will stand forever.”
i18n.he: יָבֵ֥שׁ חָצִ֖יר נָ֣בֵֽל צִ֑יץ וּדְבַר־אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ יָק֥וּם לְעוֹלָֽם׃ (ס)

paragraphs.text: עַ֣ל הַר־גָּבֹ֤הַ עֲלִי־לָךְ֙ מְבַשֶּׂ֣רֶת צִיּ֔וֹן הָרִ֤ימִי בַכֹּ֙חַ֙ קוֹלֵ֔ךְ מְבַשֶּׂ֖רֶת יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם הָרִ֙ימִי֙ אַל־תִּירָ֔אִי אִמְרִי֙ לְעָרֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה הִנֵּ֖ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם׃

i18n.en: Go up on a high mountain, you who bring good tidings to Zion; lift up your voice with strength, you who bring good tidings to Jerusalem; lift it up, do not fear; say to the cities of Judah: “Behold your God!”
i18n.he: עַ֣ל הַר־גָּבֹ֤הַ עֲלִי־לָךְ֙ מְבַשֶּׂ֣רֶת צִיּ֔וֹן הָרִ֤ימִי בַכֹּ֙חַ֙ קוֹלֵ֔ךְ מְבַשֶּׂ֖רֶת יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם הָרִ֙ימִי֙ אַל־תִּירָ֔אִי אִמְרִי֙ לְעָרֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה הִנֵּ֖ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם׃

notes.official: *mᵉḇaśśereṯ ṣiyyôn* is a feminine participle, “bearer of good tidings.” It may be an objective genitive, “you who bring good tidings to Zion” (ASV), or an apposition, “O Zion, herald of good tidings” (NRSV, NJPS), with Zion herself sent to announce the news to the cities of Judah. The feminine form slightly favours the second reading (Westermann; Blenkinsopp). The line keeps ASV and records NRSV’s reading here.

paragraphs.text: הִנֵּ֨ה אֲדֹנָ֤י יְהוִה֙ בְּחָזָ֣ק יָב֔וֹא וּזְרֹע֖וֹ מֹ֣שְׁלָה ל֑וֹ הִנֵּ֤ה שְׂכָרוֹ֙ אִתּ֔וֹ וּפְעֻלָּת֖וֹ לְפָנָֽיו׃

i18n.en: Behold, the Lord YHWH comes with might, and his arm rules for him; behold, his reward is with him, and his recompense before him.
i18n.he: הִנֵּ֨ה אֲדֹנָ֤י יְהוִה֙ בְּחָזָ֣ק יָב֔וֹא וּזְרֹע֖וֹ מֹ֣שְׁלָה ל֑וֹ הִנֵּ֤ה שְׂכָרוֹ֙ אִתּ֔וֹ וּפְעֻלָּת֖וֹ לְפָנָֽיו׃

notes.official: *ʾăḏōnāy YHWH* is “the Lord YHWH” under the overlay compound-name entry. *zᵉrōʿô mōšᵉlāh lô* “his arm rules for him”: the arm is the image of YHWH’s power in the new exodus (51:9; 52:10).

paragraphs.text: כְּרֹעֶה֙ עֶדְר֣וֹ יִרְעֶ֔ה בִּזְרֹעוֹ֙ יְקַבֵּ֣ץ טְלָאִ֔ים וּבְחֵיק֖וֹ יִשָּׂ֑א עָל֖וֹת יְנַהֵֽל׃ (ס)

i18n.en: Like a shepherd he will tend his flock; he will gather the lambs in his arm and carry them in his bosom, and gently lead those that are nursing.
i18n.he: כְּרֹעֶה֙ עֶדְר֣וֹ יִרְעֶ֔ה בִּזְרֹעוֹ֙ יְקַבֵּ֣ץ טְלָאִ֔ים וּבְחֵיק֖וֹ יִשָּׂ֑א עָל֖וֹת יְנַהֵֽל׃ (ס)

paragraphs.text: מִֽי־מָדַ֨ד בְּשָׁעֳל֜וֹ מַ֗יִם וְשָׁמַ֙יִם֙ בַּזֶּ֣רֶת תִּכֵּ֔ן וְכָ֥ל בַּשָּׁלִ֖שׁ עֲפַ֣ר הָאָ֑רֶץ וְשָׁקַ֤ל בַּפֶּ֙לֶס֙ הָרִ֔ים וּגְבָע֖וֹת בְּמֹאזְנָֽיִם׃

i18n.en: Who has measured the waters in the hollow of his hand, and marked off the skies with a span, and enclosed the dust of the earth in a measure, and weighed the mountains in scales and the hills in a balance?
i18n.he: מִֽי־מָדַ֨ד בְּשָׁעֳל֜וֹ מַ֗יִם וְשָׁמַ֙יִם֙ בַּזֶּ֣רֶת תִּכֵּ֔ן וְכָ֥ל בַּשָּׁלִ֖שׁ עֲפַ֣ר הָאָ֑רֶץ וְשָׁקַ֤ל בַּפֶּ֙לֶס֙ הָרִ֔ים וּגְבָע֖וֹת בְּמֹאזְנָֽיִם׃

notes.official: *mî-māḏaḏ bᵉšoʿŏlô mayim wᵉšāmayim bazzereṯ tikkēn* “Who has measured the waters in the hollow of his hand, and marked off the skies with a span?” The measured and stretched-out *šāmayim* of Second Isaiah’s creation hymns (40:12, 22; 42:5; 44:24; 45:12, 18; 48:13) are the physical sky as a made structure, the register of Gen 1. The central *šāmayim* rule renders that register “skies” (ASV has “heavens”). The divine-realm “heaven(s)” is kept for the dwelling of YHWH, as at 14:12–13. *tikkēn* is “mark off, regulate,” the same verb used of the spirit of YHWH in v. 13.

paragraphs.text: מִֽי־תִכֵּ֥ן אֶת־ר֖וּחַ יְהוָ֑ה וְאִ֥ישׁ עֲצָת֖וֹ יוֹדִיעֶֽנּוּ׃

i18n.en: Who has directed the spirit of YHWH, or as his counselor has taught him?
i18n.he: מִֽי־תִכֵּ֥ן אֶת־ר֖וּחַ יְהוָ֑ה וְאִ֥ישׁ עֲצָת֖וֹ יוֹדִיעֶֽנּוּ׃

notes.official: *mî-ṯikkēn ʾeṯ-rûaḥ YHWH* “Who has directed the spirit of YHWH?” *tikkēn* repeats the verb of v. 12 (“marked off the skies”): the one who measured the cosmos cannot himself be measured. ASV and NRSV have “directed”; NJPS has “plumbed the mind.” *rûaḥ YHWH* here is the divine mind or counsel, parallel to “his counselor,” and is lower-case “spirit” (NRSV, NJPS). ASV’s capital “Spirit” is not followed (overlay `ruach-divine-spirit-lower-case-isaiah`).

paragraphs.text: אֶת־מִ֤י נוֹעָץ֙ וַיְבִינֵ֔הוּ וַֽיְלַמְּדֵ֖הוּ בְּאֹ֣רַח מִשְׁפָּ֑ט וַיְלַמְּדֵ֣הוּ דַ֔עַת וְדֶ֥רֶךְ תְּבוּנ֖וֹת יוֹדִיעֶֽנּוּ׃

i18n.en: With whom did he take counsel, and who gave him understanding, and taught him in the path of justice, and taught him knowledge, and showed him the way of understanding?
i18n.he: אֶת־מִ֤י נוֹעָץ֙ וַיְבִינֵ֔הוּ וַֽיְלַמְּדֵ֖הוּ בְּאֹ֣רַח מִשְׁפָּ֑ט וַיְלַמְּדֵ֣הוּ דַ֔עַת וְדֶ֥רֶךְ תְּבוּנ֖וֹת יוֹדִיעֶֽנּוּ׃

paragraphs.text: הֵ֤ן גּוֹיִם֙ כְּמַ֣ר מִדְּלִ֔י וּכְשַׁ֥חַק מֹאזְנַ֖יִם נֶחְשָׁ֑בוּ הֵ֥ן אִיִּ֖ים כַּדַּ֥ק יִטּֽוֹל׃

i18n.en: Behold, the nations are like a drop from a bucket, and are counted as the fine dust on the scales; behold, he lifts up the coastlands like a speck.
i18n.he: הֵ֤ן גּוֹיִם֙ כְּמַ֣ר מִדְּלִ֔י וּכְשַׁ֥חַק מֹאזְנַ֖יִם נֶחְשָׁ֑בוּ הֵ֥ן אִיִּ֖ים כַּדַּ֥ק יִטּֽוֹל׃

paragraphs.text: וּלְבָנ֕וֹן אֵ֥ין דֵּ֖י בָּעֵ֑ר וְחַיָּת֔וֹ אֵ֥ין דֵּ֖י עוֹלָֽה׃ (ס)

i18n.en: And Lebanon is not enough for fuel, nor are its beasts enough for a burnt-offering.
i18n.he: וּלְבָנ֕וֹן אֵ֥ין דֵּ֖י בָּעֵ֑ר וְחַיָּת֔וֹ אֵ֥ין דֵּ֖י עוֹלָֽה׃ (ס)

paragraphs.text: כָּל־הַגּוֹיִ֖ם כְּאַ֣יִן נֶגְדּ֑וֹ מֵאֶ֥פֶס וָתֹ֖הוּ נֶחְשְׁבוּ־לֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: All the nations are as nothing before him; they are counted by him as less than nothing and emptiness.
i18n.he: כָּל־הַגּוֹיִ֖ם כְּאַ֣יִן נֶגְדּ֑וֹ מֵאֶ֥פֶס וָתֹ֖הוּ נֶחְשְׁבוּ־לֽוֹ׃

notes.official: *mē-ʾep̄es wā-ṯōhû neḥšᵉḇû-lô* “they are counted by him as less than nothing and emptiness.” Bare *tōhû* is rendered “emptiness” (ASV “vanity”) wherever it means worthlessness (also v. 23; 29:21; 44:9). The concrete “wasteland” is kept for the creation formula of 45:18 (overlay `tohu-bare-emptiness-wasteland-isaiah`).

paragraphs.text: וְאֶל־מִ֖י תְּדַמְּי֣וּן אֵ֑ל וּמַה־דְּמ֖וּת תַּ֥עַרְכוּ לֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: To whom then will you liken God, and what likeness will you set beside him?
i18n.he: וְאֶל־מִ֖י תְּדַמְּי֣וּן אֵ֑ל וּמַה־דְּמ֖וּת תַּ֥עַרְכוּ לֽוֹ׃

notes.official: *wᵉʾel-mî tᵉḏammᵉyûn ʾēl* “To whom then will you liken God?” Standalone *ʾēl* designating YHWH is “God” (ASV), the book’s practice for *ʾēl*, *ʾĕlôah* and absolute *ʾĕlōhîm* alike. The transliteration “El” of the central El-compound entries is not extended to the bare noun (overlay `elohim-el-eloah-monotheistic-formula-isaiah`). The question opens the first polemic against images (vv. 18–20).

paragraphs.text: הַפֶּ֙סֶל֙ נָסַ֣ךְ חָרָ֔שׁ וְצֹרֵ֖ף בַּזָּהָ֣ב יְרַקְּעֶ֑נּוּ וּרְתֻק֥וֹת כֶּ֖סֶף צוֹרֵֽף׃

i18n.en: The carved image! A craftsman casts it, and a goldsmith overlays it with gold, and casts silver chains for it.
i18n.he: הַפֶּ֙סֶל֙ נָסַ֣ךְ חָרָ֔שׁ וְצֹרֵ֖ף בַּזָּהָ֣ב יְרַקְּעֶ֑נּוּ וּרְתֻק֥וֹת כֶּ֖סֶף צוֹרֵֽף׃

notes.official: *hap-pesel* “the carved image!” is an exclamation answering the question of v. 18. The craftsman casts it, the goldsmith overlays it, and the silver chains hold it in place. *pesel* is “carved image” under the central `pesel-utemunah-graven-image-iconographic-prohibition-cross-corpus` entry.

paragraphs.text: הַֽמְסֻכָּ֣ן תְּרוּמָ֔ה עֵ֥ץ לֹֽא־יִרְקַ֖ב יִבְחָ֑ר חָרָ֤שׁ חָכָם֙ יְבַקֶּשׁ־ל֔וֹ לְהָכִ֥ין פֶּ֖סֶל לֹ֥א יִמּֽוֹט׃

i18n.en: As an oblation he chooses sissoo wood, wood that will not rot; he seeks out a skilled craftsman to set up a carved image that will not totter.
i18n.he: הַֽמְסֻכָּ֣ן תְּרוּמָ֔ה עֵ֥ץ לֹֽא־יִרְקַ֖ב יִבְחָ֑ר חָרָ֤שׁ חָכָם֙ יְבַקֶּשׁ־ל֔וֹ לְהָכִ֥ין פֶּ֖סֶל לֹ֥א יִמּֽוֹט׃

notes.official: *ham-mᵉsukkān tᵉrûmāh ʿēṣ lōʾ-yirqaḇ yiḇḥār* “As an oblation he chooses sissoo wood, wood that will not rot.” *mᵉsukkān* is the Akkadian loanword *musukkannu*, a durable hardwood, probably *Dalbergia sissoo*, prized for cult statues and furniture (CAD M/2 237–240; HALOT; NRSV “mulberry wood”; NJPS “mulberry”). ASV’s “he that is too impoverished for such an oblation” derives the word from *skn* “be poor,” a medieval explanation abandoned since the Akkadian word was identified. The Masoretic consonants are unchanged. *tᵉrûmāh* is “oblation,” a gift set apart for the deity, under the central `qorbanot-sacrificial-offering-vocabulary-cluster-cross-corpus` entry (overlay `lexical-cruxes-wave-i2-isaiah`).

paragraphs.text: הֲל֤וֹא תֵֽדְעוּ֙ הֲל֣וֹא תִשְׁמָ֔עוּ הֲל֛וֹא הֻגַּ֥ד מֵרֹ֖אשׁ לָכֶ֑ם הֲלוֹא֙ הֲבִ֣ינֹתֶ֔ם מוֹסְד֖וֹת הָאָֽרֶץ׃

i18n.en: Do you not know? Do you not hear? Has it not been told you from the beginning? Have you not understood from the foundations of the earth?
i18n.he: הֲל֤וֹא תֵֽדְעוּ֙ הֲל֣וֹא תִשְׁמָ֔עוּ הֲל֛וֹא הֻגַּ֥ד מֵרֹ֖אשׁ לָכֶ֑ם הֲלוֹא֙ הֲבִ֣ינֹתֶ֔ם מוֹסְד֖וֹת הָאָֽרֶץ׃

notes.official:
*hă-lôʾ hăḇînōṯem môsᵉḏôṯ hā-ʾāreṣ*. The Hebrew has no preposition before “the foundations of the earth.” ASV and NRSV supply “from,” carrying the *mē-* of the parallel *mē-rōʾš* “from the beginning” over to this clause: “Have you not understood from the foundations of the earth?” Read without that ellipsis, the phrase is the object, “Have you not understood the foundations of the earth?” NJPS gives a version of that reading (“Have you not discerned how the earth was founded?”). Both are standard readings. The line keeps the Translator’s ASV reading, and the object reading is recorded here.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** *The Book Which Tells the Truth* quotes v. 21 twice (ch. 3 and ch. 5) in the object reading (« N’avez-vous pas compris la fondation de la terre ? »), as an appeal to understand how the earth was founded. The line follows the ellipsis reading of ASV, and the object reading the canon quotes is set out above as an equally standard construal.

paragraphs.text: הַיֹּשֵׁב֙ עַל־ח֣וּג הָאָ֔רֶץ וְיֹשְׁבֶ֖יהָ כַּחֲגָבִ֑ים הַנּוֹטֶ֤ה כַדֹּק֙ שָׁמַ֔יִם וַיִּמְתָּחֵ֥ם כָּאֹ֖הֶל לָשָֽׁבֶת׃

i18n.en: It is he who sits above the circle of the earth, and its inhabitants are like grasshoppers; who stretches out the skies like a curtain, and spreads them like a tent to dwell in;
i18n.he: הַיֹּשֵׁב֙ עַל־ח֣וּג הָאָ֔רֶץ וְיֹשְׁבֶ֖יהָ כַּחֲגָבִ֑ים הַנּוֹטֶ֤ה כַדֹּק֙ שָׁמַ֔יִם וַיִּמְתָּחֵ֥ם כָּאֹ֖הֶל לָשָֽׁבֶת׃

notes.official: *ḥûḡ hā-ʾāreṣ* “the circle of the earth.” *ḥûḡ* is a circle or vault: the horizon-circle, or the dome that rests on it (Job 22:14 *ḥûḡ šāmayim* “the vault of the skies”; Prov 8:27 “he drew a circle on the face of the deep”). It describes the earth as seen from above in the ancient cosmology. It does not describe a sphere, and the line makes no claim about the earth’s shape. *šāmayim* is “skies” in the creation register (see v. 12): YHWH stretches them out “like a curtain” and spreads them “like a tent to dwell in.”

paragraphs.text: הַנּוֹתֵ֥ן רוֹזְנִ֖ים לְאָ֑יִן שֹׁ֥פְטֵי אֶ֖רֶץ כַּתֹּ֥הוּ עָשָֽׂה׃

i18n.en: who brings princes to nothing, and makes the judges of the earth like emptiness.
i18n.he: הַנּוֹתֵ֥ן רוֹזְנִ֖ים לְאָ֑יִן שֹׁ֥פְטֵי אֶ֖רֶץ כַּתֹּ֥הוּ עָשָֽׂה׃

paragraphs.text: אַ֣ף בַּל־נִטָּ֗עוּ אַ֚ף בַּל־זֹרָ֔עוּ אַ֛ף בַּל־שֹׁרֵ֥שׁ בָּאָ֖רֶץ גִּזְעָ֑ם וְגַם־נָשַׁ֤ף בָּהֶם֙ וַיִּבָ֔שׁוּ וּסְעָרָ֖ה כַּקַּ֥שׁ תִּשָּׂאֵֽם׃ (ס)

i18n.en: Scarcely are they planted, scarcely are they sown, scarcely has their stock taken root in the earth, when he blows upon them and they wither, and the storm carries them off like stubble.
i18n.he: אַ֣ף בַּל־נִטָּ֗עוּ אַ֚ף בַּל־זֹרָ֔עוּ אַ֛ף בַּל־שֹׁרֵ֥שׁ בָּאָ֖רֶץ גִּזְעָ֑ם וְגַם־נָשַׁ֤ף בָּהֶם֙ וַיִּבָ֔שׁוּ וּסְעָרָ֖ה כַּקַּ֥שׁ תִּשָּׂאֵֽם׃ (ס)

paragraphs.text: וְאֶל־מִ֥י תְדַמְּי֖וּנִי וְאֶשְׁוֶ֑ה יֹאמַ֖ר קָדֽוֹשׁ׃

i18n.en: To whom then will you liken me, that I should be equal to him? says the Holy One.
i18n.he: וְאֶל־מִ֥י תְדַמְּי֖וּנִי וְאֶשְׁוֶ֑ה יֹאמַ֖ר קָדֽוֹשׁ׃

paragraphs.text: שְׂאוּ־מָר֨וֹם עֵינֵיכֶ֤ם וּרְאוּ֙ מִי־בָרָ֣א אֵ֔לֶּה הַמּוֹצִ֥יא בְמִסְפָּ֖ר צְבָאָ֑ם לְכֻלָּם֙ בְּשֵׁ֣ם יִקְרָ֔א מֵרֹ֤ב אוֹנִים֙ וְאַמִּ֣יץ כֹּ֔חַ אִ֖ישׁ לֹ֥א נֶעְדָּֽר׃ (ס)

i18n.en: Lift up your eyes on high and see: who created these? He who brings out their host by number, who calls them all by name; by the greatness of his might, and because he is strong in power, not one is missing.
i18n.he: שְׂאוּ־מָר֨וֹם עֵינֵיכֶ֤ם וּרְאוּ֙ מִי־בָרָ֣א אֵ֔לֶּה הַמּוֹצִ֥יא בְמִסְפָּ֖ר צְבָאָ֑ם לְכֻלָּם֙ בְּשֵׁ֣ם יִקְרָ֔א מֵרֹ֤ב אוֹנִים֙ וְאַמִּ֣יץ כֹּ֔חַ אִ֖ישׁ לֹ֥א נֶעְדָּֽר׃ (ס)

notes.official:
*mî-ḇārāʾ ʾēlleh* “who created these?” — the stars, whose “host” YHWH brings out by number and calls by name. *bārāʾ* is rendered “create” throughout Isaiah (ASV, NRSV, NJPS). The draft extended the central Genesis entry `bara` (“shape”) to Isaiah, and the Editor declines the extension. In Second Isaiah the verb takes darkness, calamity, righteousness, “new things” and Jerusalem-as-a-rejoicing as objects (45:7, 8; 48:7; 65:18), never a material. It stands in parallel with *yāṣar* “form,” the potter’s verb (43:1, 7; 45:7, 18), and English “shape” would blur the contrast with “form” that the Hebrew draws (Stuhlmueller, *Creative Redemption in Deutero-Isaiah*, 1970; Westermann; Blenkinsopp, AB 19A). See overlay `bara-create-isaiah`; the decision is flagged to the founder in the wave report.

*ṣᵉḇāʾām* “their host” is the stars as an army, mustered and named; this is the astral sense of *ṣāḇāʾ* (compare 45:12).

paragraphs.text: לָ֤מָּה תֹאמַר֙ יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב וּתְדַבֵּ֖ר יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל נִסְתְּרָ֤ה דַרְכִּי֙ מֵֽיְהוָ֔ה וּמֵאֱלֹהַ֖י מִשְׁפָּטִ֥י יַעֲבֽוֹר׃

i18n.en: Why do you say, O Jacob, and speak, O Israel: “My way is hidden from YHWH, and my right is passed over by my God”?
i18n.he: לָ֤מָּה תֹאמַר֙ יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב וּתְדַבֵּ֖ר יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל נִסְתְּרָ֤ה דַרְכִּי֙ מֵֽיְהוָ֔ה וּמֵאֱלֹהַ֖י מִשְׁפָּטִ֥י יַעֲבֽוֹר׃

paragraphs.text: הֲל֨וֹא יָדַ֜עְתָּ אִם־לֹ֣א שָׁמַ֗עְתָּ אֱלֹהֵ֨י עוֹלָ֤ם ׀ יְהוָה֙ בּוֹרֵא֙ קְצ֣וֹת הָאָ֔רֶץ לֹ֥א יִיעַ֖ף וְלֹ֣א יִיגָ֑ע אֵ֥ין חֵ֖קֶר לִתְבוּנָתֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: Do you not know? Have you not heard? The everlasting God, YHWH, the Creator of the ends of the earth, does not faint or grow weary; his understanding is unsearchable.
i18n.he: הֲל֨וֹא יָדַ֜עְתָּ אִם־לֹ֣א שָׁמַ֗עְתָּ אֱלֹהֵ֨י עוֹלָ֤ם ׀ יְהוָה֙ בּוֹרֵא֙ קְצ֣וֹת הָאָ֔רֶץ לֹ֥א יִיעַ֖ף וְלֹ֣א יִיגָ֑ע אֵ֥ין חֵ֖קֶר לִתְבוּנָתֽוֹ׃

notes.official: *ʾĕlōhê ʿôlām YHWH bôrēʾ qᵉṣôṯ hā-ʾāreṣ* “The everlasting God, YHWH, the Creator of the ends of the earth.” The participle *bôrēʾ* is rendered as a title, “the Creator” (ASV), because it stands in apposition to the divine name (overlay `bara-create-isaiah`). *ʾĕlōhê ʿôlām* “the everlasting God” is a construct epithet, rendered under the overlay pattern for construct *ʾĕlōhîm*. Compare *ʾēl ʿôlām* at Gen 21:33, transliterated “El Olam” by the central compound entry, which is a different construction.

paragraphs.text: נֹתֵ֥ן לַיָּעֵ֖ף כֹּ֑חַ וּלְאֵ֥ין אוֹנִ֖ים עָצְמָ֥ה יַרְבֶּֽה׃

i18n.en: He gives power to the faint, and to him who has no might he increases strength.
i18n.he: נֹתֵ֥ן לַיָּעֵ֖ף כֹּ֑חַ וּלְאֵ֥ין אוֹנִ֖ים עָצְמָ֥ה יַרְבֶּֽה׃

paragraphs.text: וְיִֽעֲפ֥וּ נְעָרִ֖ים וְיִגָ֑עוּ וּבַחוּרִ֖ים כָּשׁ֥וֹל יִכָּשֵֽׁלוּ׃

i18n.en: Even youths shall faint and be weary, and young men shall stumble and fall;
i18n.he: וְיִֽעֲפ֥וּ נְעָרִ֖ים וְיִגָ֑עוּ וּבַחוּרִ֖ים כָּשׁ֥וֹל יִכָּשֵֽׁלוּ׃

paragraphs.text: וְקוֹיֵ֤ יְהוָה֙ יַחֲלִ֣יפוּ כֹ֔חַ יַעֲל֥וּ אֵ֖בֶר כַּנְּשָׁרִ֑ים יָר֙וּצוּ֙ וְלֹ֣א יִיגָ֔עוּ יֵלְכ֖וּ וְלֹ֥א יִיעָֽפוּ׃ (פ)

i18n.en: but those who wait for YHWH shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings like eagles; they shall run and not be weary; they shall walk and not faint.
i18n.he: וְקוֹיֵ֤ יְהוָה֙ יַחֲלִ֣יפוּ כֹ֔חַ יַעֲל֥וּ אֵ֖בֶר כַּנְּשָׁרִ֑ים יָר֙וּצוּ֙ וְלֹ֣א יִיגָ֔עוּ יֵלְכ֖וּ וְלֹ֥א יִיעָֽפוּ׃ (פ)
